title: TMTG ETFs, TAE fusion merger, TMTG losses
summary: Trump Media's Truth.Fi brand launched five Truth Social ETFs on 2025-12-30, including the three the video names. TMTG announced an all-stock merger with fusion developer TAE Technologies valued at more than $6B on 2025-12-18. FY2025 revenue was about $3.7M against a net loss of $712.3M, and DJT stock is near multi-year lows. Several details are off: the ETFs are thematic baskets, not an 'S&P 500 but not woke'; the $712M loss was mostly unrealized crypto markdowns and dates from 2025 (Q3 2026 showed a $410M paper profit); and the TAE deal is still pending, with a vote set for 2026-12-14.

sub_claims.statement: TMTG sells Truth Social American Security & Defense, American Next Frontiers and American Icons ETFs that are basically a non-woke S&P 500.
sub_claims.finding: Confirmed: TSSD, TSNF/TSFN and TSIC launched on NYSE on 2025-12-30 as part of a five-fund Truth.Fi slate. Yorkville America Equities is the adviser and Tuttle Capital is the subadviser, with anti-DEI / America-first screening. They are not S&P 500 clones: each is a narrow thematic basket, and early assets totaled about $46M.

sub_claims.statement: TMTG announced a ~$6B all-stock merger with fusion company TAE Technologies.
sub_claims.finding: Announced 2025-12-18 as an all-stock deal valued at more than $6B, with roughly a 50/50 ownership split and up to $200M + $100M in cash from TMTG to TAE. As of 2026-11-14 it has not closed: the S-4 became effective 2026-11-05, the shareholder vote is 2026-12-14 and the outside date is 2026-12-18. Nunes, slated as co-CEO, left as TMTG CEO on 2026-04-21.

sub_claims.statement: Fusion is not commercially viable yet and depends heavily on regulation and government approval.
sub_claims.finding: No fusion company sells commercial power. The planned 50 MWe plant is 'subject to required approvals', and filings say there is no obligation to build it. Richard Painter (via the Washington Post) and Axios both flagged the regulatory dependence and conflict risk. TAE's CEO lobbied DOE for federal funding days before the announcement. The 'commentator' in the video is unnamed.
Down about 70% in 2025 before the TAE pop. Late October 2026 it traded around $5.8-6.4, near its 52-week low (52-week high about $17).

sub_claims.statement: Revenues are a few million dollars against $712 million in losses.
sub_claims.finding: FY2025: revenue of about $3.7M and a net loss of $712.3M (10-K filed 2026-02-27). The loss was mostly non-cash, including $403.2M in digital-asset markdowns, and operating cash flow was +$14.8M. In Q3 2026 TMTG reported $409.7M of net income on $3.0M revenue from crypto gains; the nine-month 2026 net loss was about $234.2M.

sub_claims.statement: The losses were funded by the president's most diehard supporters.
sub_claims.finding: This is a characterization. Retail investors are prominent in DJT, but much of TMTG's capital came from a roughly $2.4B institutional raise in 2025. No source quantifies supporter funding.

corrections: Transcript says 'Tay Technologies Inc'; the company is TAE Technologies.
Video calls the ETFs 'basically the S&P 500, but not woke'; they are narrow thematic, screened baskets (defense, frontier tech, iconic brands) from a five-fund lineup.
The $712M loss is the FY2025 figure and was mostly unrealized crypto markdowns. Q3 2026 showed a ~$410M paper profit, and the nine-month 2026 loss is ~$234M.
The TAE merger is announced but not completed: the shareholder vote is 2026-12-14. Devin Nunes, the planned co-CEO, stepped down as TMTG CEO in April 2026.
denials_and_context: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said neither the President nor his family have ever engaged, or will ever engage, in conflicts of interest.
Trump's TMTG shares are held in a revocable trust managed by Donald Trump Jr., who sits on TMTG's board.
Richard Painter noted the criminal conflict-of-interest statute does not cover the president, so the deal is legal even if ethically fraught.

TAE is a long-running private fusion company (backed by Alphabet, among others) and existed well before the Trump administration; Rep. Don Beyer noted that more than two dozen US fusion firms exist, some further along.
The ETFs are run by Yorkville America Equities and Tuttle Capital under a Truth.Fi brand license; TMTG is not the fund manager.
